result.summary: This PR changes CDBWrapper's LevelDB options so that on 64-bit builds, where mmap makes table blocks non-cacheable, the block cache is given zero capacity instead of half the dbcache budget, and that freed half is moved into the write buffer instead. 32-bit builds keep the existing block-cache/write-buffer split since mmap is disabled there. The change is backed by benchmarks on SSD and HDD across multiple machines, none showing a clear win.
result.problem: CDBWrapper currently reserves half of each index/chainstate DB's cache budget for LevelDB's block cache, but on 64-bit builds LevelDB serves uncompressed table blocks via mmap and marks them non-cacheable, so that half of the configured dbcache is effectively wasted and unavailable for anything useful.

open_concerns: sedited questioned whether keeping special-case code for 32-bit builds is worth it versus just using the LevelDB default write buffer size, and asked if there's any benefit to giving indexes more than the default write buffer

Author's own HDD benchmarks are mixed/inconclusive, and author says more investigation is needed into whether any path still uses the block cache or write buffers as expected

categories.name: indexes
categories.evidence: Directly modifies src/dbwrapper.cpp, the shared LevelDB wrapper used by chainstate and all optional indexes, changing how cache memory is allocated between block cache and write buffers.
categories.rationale: Benchmarks across SSD (Ryzen, i9) and HDD (i7) machines and an ARM (RPi5) machine show no meaningful reindex-chainstate speedup, ratios all within ~1-3%, some slightly worse on HDD. The change reallocates already-wasted memory rather than adding new capacity, so the ceiling on benefit is small; author's own words: 'no meaningful runtime change.' It is real correctness-adjacent tidying of dbcache accounting but not a fix for a bug or a clear performance win yet.

result.card: This draft PR changes CDBWrapper's LevelDB options so 64-bit builds give the block cache zero capacity (since mmap makes table blocks non-cacheable there) and move that freed budget into the write buffer instead, while 32-bit builds keep the old split. The problem is that dbcache memory is silently wasted on the block cache on 64-bit builds, which affects chainstate and every index built on CDBWrapper. The author's own benchmarks across SSD, HDD, and ARM machines show no meaningful runtime change, undercutting the performance case. Reviewer sedited suggested a simpler fix, dropping the 32-bit special case entirely and just using LevelDB's default write buffer size, and the author agreed to consider a bigger rewrite, marking the PR draft pending further investigation into whether any code path still depends on the block cache. No dependency on other PRs, but it lightly conflicts with open PR #35568 which also touches disk usage optimization for an index.
